references.title: Set Kubelet Parameters Via A Configuration File

steps: Inspect the operator-supplied kubelet podPidsLimit, source node and currentness; one record does not establish coverage of other nodes.
With the node owner, choose a positive limit that fits expected Pod process counts and update the owning kubelet configuration or node-pool IaC.
Roll out by node group with workload disruption planning; verify the effective per-node setting and restore the prior node configuration if the approved capacity criteria fail.
k8s.cis.a_limit_is_set_on_pod_pids.summary: Set a positive Pod PID limit on the applicable kubelet configuration after capacity review.

steps: Inspect the operator-attested feature gate and kubelet release; an omitted gate on a current release can be default-enabled and is not proof of disabled rotation.

With the node and certificate owners, verify serverTLSBootstrap and a security-reviewed serving-certificate CSR approver before setting the gate true in the owned kubelet configuration where supported.
Roll out safely and verify approved CSRs and issued serving certificates independently; restore the prior configuration if bootstrap or node availability fails.
k8s.cis.kubelet_rotate_kubelet_server_ce.summary: Review an explicit disabled kubelet serving-certificate rotation gate with bootstrap and CSR approval prerequisites.

steps: Inspect the operator-attested kubelet seccompDefault field, applicable kubelet release and workload overrides; a missing field does not prove false.
With the node owner, test RuntimeDefault compatibility and set seccompDefault=true in the owned kubelet configuration for applicable nodes.
Roll out node by node, verify effective seccomp behavior without assuming declaration equals enforcement, and restore the prior configuration if workloads fail.
k8s.cis.the_seccomp_default_parameter_is.summary: Declare seccompDefault=true in the applicable kubelet configuration after workload compatibility review.
